label: Chapter
summary: A period of your life turned into a memoir chapter — a bounded stretch of time with its own shape, key scenes, and a turning point.

slots.label: Foundation
slots.description: Name and bound the chapter — what you'd title it, how it began, how it ended.

slots.label: Life Structure
slots.description: The pillars of those years — work, relationships, home, a guiding Dream — which was the keystone and what was neglected.

slots.label: Central Scene
slots.description: A typical day, waking to sleeping, and the sensory texture of the period — where you lived, what things cost, the music, the rooms.

slots.label: Turning Point
slots.description: The key scenes — a high point, a low point, a turning point — each with what happened, who was there, what you felt, what it says about you.

slots.label: Transition Out
slots.description: The change itself and the inner transition — when it ended inside you, what you let go of, and the neutral zone between the old life and the new.

slots.label: Look Back
slots.description: The later evaluative pass — how you make peace with this chapter now and what it gave you that you only see from here.

research.basis: Slots implement the synthesized six-step period arc (research.md §4): McAdams's table-of-contents naming, Levinson's life-structure/Dream construct, oral-history typical-day reconstruction, McAdams's five-slot key-scene probe, Bridges's two-layer transition (ending + neutral zone), and Butler's evaluative life-review pass — the step with the strongest well-being evidence.
citations: McAdams & McLean 2013 — narrative identity chapters and eight key scenes (high point, low point, turning point) organize autobiographical recall
Levinson 1978 — 'life structure' and 'the Dream' as an organizing developmental construct that is pursued, modified, or abandoned across a period
Bridges 1980 — transitions have three phases: an ending, a neutral zone, and a new beginning; the neutral zone is the most under-captured memoir material
Butler 1963 — the evaluative 'life review' integration pass carries the strongest meta-analytic support for well-being gain, more than recall alone

ai_context: When the key scenes carry a redemption arc (hardship into growth), let it surface in the look-back reflection — never impose the frame if the source material doesn't offer it.
Anchor time relative to life landmarks (a move, a birth, a job change) rather than calendar years when the source itself doesn't give a date.
Track 'the Dream' (a guiding ambition for the period) if present in the material — whether it was pursued, modified, or let go — without editorializing on which was the right outcome.
